bayts.text: I have turned my face to Him (Allah) whose honouring is manifest, in the month of the birth of him (the Prophet Muḥammad) through whom He sustained us upon the sea.
To God my thanksgiving, here, in the month of Rabīʿ (al-Awwal), for my undertaking of what He has chosen for me as a votive offering.
Already good has come from Him (Allah) who has no partner in sovereignty or in praise, in secret and in the open.
I have called upon the Kind (Al-Barr), the Most Merciful (Ar-Raḥīm): how excellent He who has honoured us on land and sea! How excellent is God, our Master!
By Your "Be!" (Kun) bring into being for me, on this day, an abundance of means, that I may raise pillars for the religion of God.
You have nurtured me: so grant me, this year, O my Everlasting Refuge (Aṣ-Ṣamad), perseverance (idmān) in good, felicity and a peaceful abode.
You have nurtured me after feeding me and giving me drink, since the Day of Tarwiya (the 8th of Dhū l-Ḥijja), when I wandered thirsty.
You have made me firm after hardship, You have led to me fine garments, widening all things after I had been held back, bereft.
Today I have addressed You in intimate prayer, O You who honoured me yesterday, and today You have led to me certainty and clear proof.
Turn the hearts of the Nazarenes (the Christian colonisers), O All-Powerful, to my aid, and subdue for me whoever is mighty or weak.
Since You are the One (Al-Wāḥid), the Subduer (Al-Qahhār), alone and without peer, subdue our enemies for me, so that my glad tidings may endure.
Yesterday You roused me with a warning in which I behold a marvel: You are the Originator (Al-Badīʿ), who never ceases to be the All-Merciful (Ar-Raḥmān).
Yesterday You made all easy for me: grant me today an abundance through which I may persevere, with excellence, in what pleases You.
You gave me refuge after my heart had been straitened by harm: so subdue for me, forever, jinn and men.
I have surrendered my face to You today, as a servant of him (Muḥammad) for whom I have become a Kaʿb and a Ḥassān (the Prophet's poets).
My ink has called for the fulfilment of my need, for the service of him (Muḥammad) whose glad tidings made us forget the enemies' harm:
Muḥammad, the best of God's creatures, our master; may He (Allah) whom I call upon for clarity send blessing upon him.
Turn to him (Muḥammad) forever a blessing joined with peace, to me the clarity of eloquence, and hold disobedience far from me.
You have carried me, O Lord, with honour, without hardship, over land and sea: increase my provision and my trust in You.
Grant me possession, this year, O Bestower (Al-Wahhāb), beyond my hope, and subdue for me hostility and whatever consoles the foe.
Grant me a lawful and pure provision, and preserve me from what You do not approve, in secret and in the open.
I have addressed my intimate prayer to the Kind, the Most Merciful, the Enricher (Allah); to Him I entrust my affair, and I hope, even now, for His help.
Accept my thanksgiving, widen my means here and hereafter, O Vast (Al-Wāsiʿ), O Enricher, who never cease to be the Supreme Judge (Ad-Dayyān).
Grant me, from Your cup, O Bestower, all my wishes together, until I am quenched with the water of the Unseen (al-ghayb).
Make me firm and widen my means, and let my sojourn (mukthī) be in abundance, like the Night of Destiny (Laylat al-Qadr), time after time.
In You make my sojourn a self-extinction (fanāʾ) without any slip, and through me bring to perfection eminent souls, and yet more eminent souls.
Make good easy for me, protect me and increase my right guidance, O Bestower of benefit, who never cease to be Kind and Bestower of favours (Al-Mannān).
Yours my heart and my body, and likewise my hand, O Guide (Al-Hādī), who never cease to be Lord and Most Tender (Al-Ḥannān).
Grant me without delay the meeting with the people of faith, that You may gladden whoever was grieving.
Since You are the Subduer (Al-Qāhir), the Compeller (Al-Jabbār), I have asked here that I need not contend with a tyrant or a sovereign.
